name: VACTERL Association

criteria.description: Presence of vertebral anomalies such as hemivertebrae or fused vertebrae
Imperforate anus or other anorectal malformations
Congenital heart defects including ventricular septal defect or tetralogy of Fallot
Renal structural anomalies such as renal agenesis or dysplasia
Radial aplasia, hypoplastic thumbs, or other limb abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least three of the characteristic congenital malformations involving vertebral, anal, cardiac, tracheoesophageal, renal, or limb anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; no single genetic cause identified. Exclusion of other syndromes is important.

common.symptomName: Limb abnormalities (e.g., radial aplasia, hypoplastic thumbs)
Feeding difficulties due to esophageal anomalies

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory distress secondary to tracheal anomalies
Urinary tract infections due to renal malformations

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: Contrast studies demonstrating tracheoesophageal fistula or esophageal atresia
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; mostly sporadic cases
Rare familial cases reported with possible multifactorial inheritance
other: Clinical diagnosis based on constellation of malformations
Exclusion of other syndromes with overlapping features (e.g., CHARGE, Fanconi anemia)

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress due to tracheoesophageal fistula
Critical congenital heart defects causing cyanosis
Renal failure or severe urinary tract malformations
references: Solomon BD, Pineda-Alvarez DE, Raam MS. VACTERL/VATER Association. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.

Carmichael SL, Shaw GM. Maternal life event stress and congenital anomalies. Epidemiology. 2000;11(1):30-35.
